channel.title: Shahid Moosa — Distributed Systems Engineering
channel.description: Deep dives into distributed databases, query optimization, and production infrastructure.

item.title: Out-of-Memory No More: Parsing 10GB Database Diagnostic Bundles Locally
item.description: How I built S2 Report Sniffer's bounded-memory stream processing engine to ingest massive distributed database logs without crashing.

item.title: Understanding CAP Theorem in Production
item.description: A practical guide to navigating consistency, availability, and partition tolerance trade-offs when architecting distributed databases.

item.title: Pragmatic Consistency: When Stronger Isn't Better
item.description: The case against defaulting to strict serializability. Mapping business requirements to the lowest viable consistency level for maximum scalability.

item.title: The Latency Tax of Separated Compute and Storage
item.description: A critical analysis of disaggregated storage architectures vs shared-nothing systems. Examining network I/O penalties and why caching layers fail for high-concurrency point lookups.

item.title: Surviving Data Skew in Distributed Joins
item.description: How uneven data distribution destroys shuffle join performance. Contrasting broadcast joins vs repartitioning and why query optimizers often miss skew.

item.title: Non-Blocking DDL is a Myth: Schema Evolution at Scale
item.description: How lock propagation and metadata sync cause latency spikes even in 'online' DDL. Defensive patterns for schema migration using expansion/contraction strategies.

item.title: Defensive Ingestion: Managing Backpressure in HTAP Systems
item.description: Protecting HTAP systems from ingestion floods. Why Kafka alone isn't enough and how to implement database-aware flow control.

item.title: Query Optimization at Petabyte Scale
item.description: Lessons learned from debugging slow queries across distributed nodes. Execution plans, index strategies, and memory management.

item.title: Incident Response for Database Engineers
item.description: A battle-tested playbook for handling production database incidents. From detection to resolution to post-mortem.

item.title: Sharding Strategies That Actually Work
item.description: Comparing hash, range, and geo-based sharding with real performance benchmarks and migration patterns.

item.title: Lessons Learned Running SingleStore in Production
item.description: Real-world lessons from operating SingleStore clusters—from memory sizing and query pitfalls to silent failures and what I'd do differently next time.

item.title: Understanding the SingleStore Execution Engine
item.description: A field guide to SingleStore's execution engine—how aggregators and leaves work, why data movement is expensive, and how to read an execution plan like a detective.

item.title: Why Indexes Everywhere Is a Bad Strategy
item.description: Indexes look like free speed—until they quietly tax every write, consume memory, and evict the data you actually need.

item.title: Your Database Is Probably Fine
item.description: Most outages blamed on the database aren't the database's fault—they're query-shape problems in disguise.

item.title: When Vertical Scaling Beats Horizontal
item.description: Horizontal scale sounds heroic—until you realize it adds failure modes, latency, and complexity your workload never needed.
